beachrain

Does rain affect my beach? beachrain helps Sydney swimmers see whether bacteria levels at their beach tend to rise after rain and how their beach compares with other nearby beaches.

Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-abhignatippala/

What’s in the package

Component What it does
beach_samples 36,062 enterococci samples from 77 Sydney swim sites (2015 to 2025), each matched to the rain that fell in the previous 72 hours
sydney_rainfall Daily Sydney rainfall and temperature used to build the 72-hour totals
summarise_exceedance() Share of samples above a bacteria threshold in each rainfall band
compare_sites() Ranks swim sites by how much rain changes their water quality
plot_exceedance() Bar chart of a beach’s summary beside its region
run_app() Launches the Rain Check Shiny app

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/YOUR-REPO-NAME")

Launch the app 

library(beachrain)
run_app()

The app is designed for Sydney swimmers who want to know how rain might affect their usual beach. Choose your beach and the bacteria level you want to check. The chart then shows how your beach (blue) compares with other beaches in the same region (beige) across four different levels of rainfall.

A quick example 

library(beachrain)

bondi <- beach_samples[beach_samples$swim_site == "Bondi Beach", ]
summarise_exceedance(bondi, threshold = 40)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   rain_band                 n_samples n_exceed prop_exceed few_samples
#>   <fct>                         <int>    <int>       <dbl> <lgl>      
#> 1 "Dry\n(under 1 mm)"             215        8      0.0372 FALSE      
#> 2 "Light\n(1 to 10 mm)"           238       26      0.109  FALSE      
#> 3 "Moderate\n(10 to 25 mm)"        89       15      0.169  FALSE      
#> 4 "Heavy\n(25 mm or more)"         52       15      0.288  FALSE

Compare prop_exceed in the Dry row with the Heavy row: the gap shows how much heavy rain raises the chance of poor water quality at Bondi.

Data

  • Water quality: Beachwatch NSW, NSW Government, https://www.beachwatch.nsw.gov.au/waterMonitoring/waterQualityData
  • Weather: Open-Meteo historical weather API, licensed under CC BY 4.0, https://open-meteo.com/

Both datasets were curated for TidyTuesday (20 May 2025) by Jen Richmond (R-Ladies Sydney). The script data-raw/beach_samples.R downloads the raw files and reproduces the package data.

Generative AI declaration

Generative AI declaration: I used Claude (Anthropic) for some parts of the package development, mainly to get help with the Shiny app, CSS styling, package configuration and a few technical aspects of the documentation. I used its suggestions as a starting point and made my own changes to the code, app layout, title, wording and colour theme. I also rewrote the vignette and README, tested the package and reviewed the final work to make sure I understood how everything worked.
